subject.title: [Bug]: Slack replies ~2s slower than other channels — dominant cost is Socket Mode event delivery; channel-side stalls fixed in #101888

question: Should this issue be resolved with latency-aware Slack docs/setup guidance for HTTP Request URLs, or should OpenClaw change Slack setup/default behavior beyond the existing `mode: "http"` support?
rationale: HTTP mode already exists and Slack recommends HTTP for deployed production/team apps, but changing setup or defaults would affect operators who currently rely on Socket Mode for private or local deployments.

options.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
options.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default and update Slack docs/setup guidance to prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

options.title: Change setup or defaults
options.body: Have maintainers sponsor a stronger setup/default change that steers new hosted Slack installs toward HTTP mode, with upgrade and operator guidance.

options.title: Accept current guidance
options.body: Decide the current transport table is sufficient and close only after recording that no additional latency-specific docs or setup change is planned.

recommendation.title: Document HTTP latency guidance
recommendation.body: Keep Socket Mode as the default and update Slack docs/setup guidance to prefer HTTP Request URLs for hosted public-ingress deployments where reply latency matters.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided the measurement, authored the partial Slack latency fixes, and explicitly scoped the remaining HTTP-guidance decision.
